problem_text:
A logistics coordinator is tasked with allocating a set of shipments into identical cargo planes. The shipments are as follows:

* Shipment Alpha: mass 69 tons
* Shipment Beta: mass 69 tons
* Shipment Gamma: mass 43 tons
* Shipment Delta: mass 65 tons
* Shipment Epsilon: mass 62 tons
* Shipment Zeta: mass 49 tons
* Shipment Eta: mass 63 tons
* Shipment Theta: mass 45 tons
* Shipment Iota: mass 40 tons
* Shipment Kappa: mass 41 tons
* Shipment Lambda: mass 52 tons
* Shipment Mu: mass 34 tons
* Shipment Nu: mass 36 tons
* Shipment Xi: mass 48 tons
* Shipment Omicron: mass 56 tons
* Shipment Pi: mass 57 tons
* Shipment Rho: mass 62 tons
* Shipment Sigma: mass 46 tons
* Shipment Tau: mass 63 tons
* Shipment Upsilon: mass 39 tons
* Shipment Phi: mass 37 tons
* Shipment Chi: mass 53 tons
* Shipment Psi: mass 55 tons
* Shipment Omega: mass 37 tons
* Shipment Ares: mass 41 tons
* Shipment Boreas: mass 33 tons
* Shipment Cronus: mass 56 tons
* Shipment Demeter: mass 65 tons
* Shipment Eos: mass 31 tons
* Shipment Helios: mass 66 tons
* Shipment Iris: mass 47 tons
* Shipment Janus: mass 66 tons
* Shipment Krios: mass 50 tons
* Shipment Leto: mass 45 tons
* Shipment Metis: mass 31 tons
* Shipment Nyx: mass 33 tons

Each aircraft has a maximum payload capacity of 100 tons. The coordinator must assign every shipment to exactly one aircraft, ensuring the combined mass on any plane does not surpass its limit. The objective is to utilize the smallest possible fleet of aircraft to accommodate all shipments.
